mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving average signals weakening aggregate demand but a nascent recovery in residential investment, which historically precedes a mild positive equity correction over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > 12-month MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately compressing corporate margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate lower earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over three months signals a precautionary savings behavior, which typically precedes a market drawdown as consumers delay discretionary spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 3-month moving average AND GDPC1 < 3-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held steady at or below 2% for six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports corporate borrowing and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS <= 2.0% for 6 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 3.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically greater than zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payrolls increase (PAYEMS) below the average monthly growth of the previous 12 months for three consecutive months signals decelerating labor market momentum, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate slower revenue growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 12-month average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below its 6-month moving average while the unemployment rate remains below 4% signals a housing-specific demand shock in a tight labor market, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days due to sectoral drag on earnings.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 6-month MA AND UNRATE < 4.0% for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: tight labor market with housing weakness
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
